import pandas as pd

# Load intermediate join results as per operation history and intermediate files
# intermediate_step1: join of Source6_98_0 and Source6_98_1 on Id
intermediate_step1 = pd.read_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_98/intermediate_step1.csv"
)

# intermediate_step2: join of Source6_98_2 and Source6_98_3 on Id
intermediate_step2 = pd.read_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_98/intermediate_step2.csv"
)

# intermediate_step3: join of Source6_98_4 and Source6_98_5 on Id
intermediate_step3 = pd.read_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_98/intermediate_step3.csv"
)

# intermediate_step4: join of Source6_98_6 and Source6_98_1 on Id
intermediate_step4 = pd.read_csv(
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length6_98/intermediate_step4.csv"
)

# We have these intermediate tables:
# intermediate_step1: ['Unnamed: 0', 'Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y']
# intermediate_step2: ['Id', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4']
# intermediate_step3: ['Id', 'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6']
# intermediate_step4: ['Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y']

# The target schema is:
# ['Id': int,
#  'SalePrice_x': float,
#  'SalePrice_y': float,
#  'SalePrice_x_3': float,
#  'SalePrice_y_4': float,
#  'SalePrice_x_5': float,
#  'SalePrice_y_6': float,
#  'SalePrice': float]

# We need to join all these intermediate tables on 'Id' to get all columns together.

# First, drop 'Unnamed: 0' from intermediate_step1 as it is an index column from CSV
intermediate_step1 = intermediate_step1.drop(columns=['Unnamed: 0'])

# Join intermediate_step1 and intermediate_step2 on 'Id'
df = pd.merge(intermediate_step1, intermediate_step2, on='Id', how='inner')

# Join the result with intermediate_step3 on 'Id'
df = pd.merge(df, intermediate_step3, on='Id', how='inner')

# Join the result with intermediate_step4 on 'Id'
# Note: intermediate_step4 has SalePrice_x and SalePrice_y columns, which will cause suffixes
# We already have SalePrice_x and SalePrice_y from intermediate_step1.
# To avoid confusion, rename columns in intermediate_step4 before join.

intermediate_step4_renamed = intermediate_step4.rename(
    columns={'SalePrice_x': 'SalePrice_x_4', 'SalePrice_y': 'SalePrice_y_4_2'}
)

# Join on 'Id'
df = pd.merge(df, intermediate_step4_renamed, on='Id', how='inner')

# Now, the target columns are:
# 'Id',
# 'SalePrice_x' (from intermediate_step1),
# 'SalePrice_y' (from intermediate_step1),
# 'SalePrice_x_3' (from intermediate_step2),
# 'SalePrice_y_4' (from intermediate_step2),
# 'SalePrice_x_5' (from intermediate_step3),
# 'SalePrice_y_6' (from intermediate_step3),
# 'SalePrice' (final column)

# The intermediate_step4 columns 'SalePrice_x_4' and 'SalePrice_y_4_2' are not part of target schema,
# so we will drop them.

df = df.drop(columns=['SalePrice_x_4', 'SalePrice_y_4_2'])

# The final column 'SalePrice' is not present in any intermediate table.
# From the target examples and the operation history, it is likely that 'SalePrice' is computed
# as the average of all SalePrice_x and SalePrice_y columns or some combination.

# Let's compute 'SalePrice' as the average of all SalePrice columns available:
# SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y, SalePrice_x_3, SalePrice_y_4, SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6

saleprice_cols = [
    'SalePrice_x',
    'SalePrice_y',
    'SalePrice_x_3',
    'SalePrice_y_4',
    'SalePrice_x_5',
    'SalePrice_y_6',
]

df['SalePrice'] = df[saleprice_cols].mean(axis=1)

# Ensure column order as per target schema
target_columns = [
    'Id',
    'SalePrice_x',
    'SalePrice_y',
    'SalePrice_x_3',
    'SalePrice_y_4',
    'SalePrice_x_5',
    'SalePrice_y_6',
    'SalePrice',
]

df = df[target_columns]

# Cast types to match target schema
df = df.astype({
    'Id': 'int64',
    'SalePrice_x': 'float64',
    'SalePrice_y': 'float64',
    'SalePrice_x_3': 'float64',
    'SalePrice_y_4': 'float64',
    'SalePrice_x_5': 'float64',
    'SalePrice_y_6': 'float64',
    'SalePrice': 'float64',
})

# Save to the target path
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read all source CSVs with index_col=0
s0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
s1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
s2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
s3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
s4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
s5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_5.csv", index_col=0)
s6 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/training_6.csv", index_col=0)

# Join pairs of sources on Id, suffixes to avoid column name conflicts
join0 = pd.merge(s0, s1, on="Id", suffixes=("_x", "_y"))
join1 = pd.merge(s2, s3, on="Id", suffixes=("_x_3", "_y_4"))
join2 = pd.merge(s4, s5, on="Id", suffixes=("_x_5", "_y_6"))
join3 = pd.merge(s6, s1, on="Id", suffixes=("_y_6", "_y"))  # s1 reused here, but will be merged later

# Now join join0 and join1 on Id
join4 = pd.merge(join0, join1, on="Id")

# Join join2 and join3 on Id
join5 = pd.merge(join2, join3, on="Id")

# Join join4 and join5 on Id to get all columns together
full_join = pd.merge(join4, join5, on="Id")

# The resulting dataframe has duplicated columns from s1 in join0 and join3 (SalePrice_y and SalePrice_y_y)
# We need to rename columns to match target schema exactly:
# Target schema: ['Id', 'SalePrice_x', 'SalePrice_y', 'SalePrice_x_3', 'SalePrice_y_4', 'SalePrice_x_5', 'SalePrice_y_6', 'SalePrice']

# Columns from join0: SalePrice_x (from s0), SalePrice_y (from s1)
# Columns from join1: SalePrice_x_3 (from s2), SalePrice_y_4 (from s3)
# Columns from join2: SalePrice_x_5 (from s4), SalePrice_y_6 (from s5)
# Columns from join3: SalePrice_y_6 (from s6), SalePrice_y (from s1 again) - duplicated s1 columns

# To avoid confusion, we will drop duplicated s1 columns from join3 (keep only SalePrice from s6 as SalePrice_y_6)
# But join3 columns have suffixes _y_6 and _y, so SalePrice_y_6 is from s6, SalePrice_y is from s1 again

# Drop SalePrice_y column from join3 to avoid duplication
join3.drop(columns=["SalePrice_y"], inplace=True)

# Re-merge join2 and join3 again after dropping duplicated column
join5 = pd.merge(join2, join3, on="Id")

# Re-merge join4 and join5
full_join = pd.merge(join4, join5, on="Id")

# Now full_join columns:
# Id
# SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y (from join0)
# SalePrice_x_3, SalePrice_y_4 (from join1)
# SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6 (from join2)
# SalePrice_y_6 (from join3) - duplicated column name, rename to SalePrice_y_6_6 to avoid conflict

# Rename duplicated SalePrice_y_6 column from join3 to SalePrice_y_6_6 temporarily
if "SalePrice_y_6" in join3.columns and "SalePrice_y_6" in join2.columns:
    join3.rename(columns={"SalePrice_y_6": "SalePrice_y_6_6"}, inplace=True)

# Rebuild join5 and full_join with updated join3
join5 = pd.merge(join2, join3, on="Id")
full_join = pd.merge(join4, join5, on="Id")

# Now full_join columns:
# Id
# SalePrice_x, SalePrice_y
# SalePrice_x_3, SalePrice_y_4
# SalePrice_x_5, SalePrice_y_6
# SalePrice_y_6_6

# The target schema has only one SalePrice_y_6 column, so we need to aggregate these two SalePrice_y_6 columns (from s5 and s6)
# The target SalePrice column is presumably the average or some aggregate of all SalePrice columns

# Aggregate by Id, taking mean of all SalePrice columns except Id
agg_df = full_join.groupby("Id").agg({
    "SalePrice_x": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_3": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_4": "mean",
    "SalePrice_x_5": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_6": "mean",
    "SalePrice_y_6_6": "mean"
}).reset_index()

# Combine the two SalePrice_y_6 columns by averaging them into one column SalePrice_y_6
agg_df["SalePrice_y_6"] = agg_df[["SalePrice_y_6", "SalePrice_y_6_6"]].mean(axis=1)

# Drop the temporary SalePrice_y_6_6 column
agg_df.drop(columns=["SalePrice_y_6_6"], inplace=True)

# Compute final SalePrice as mean of all SalePrice columns (excluding Id)
agg_df["SalePrice"] = agg_df[[
    "SalePrice_x", "SalePrice_y", "SalePrice_x_3", "SalePrice_y_4", "SalePrice_x_5", "SalePrice_y_6"
]].mean(axis=1)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
agg_df = agg_df[[
    "Id", "SalePrice_x", "SalePrice_y", "SalePrice_x_3", "SalePrice_y_4", "SalePrice_x_5", "SalePrice_y_6", "SalePrice"
]]

# Write output CSV without index
agg_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_98/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
